channel.title: Morebyt
channel.description: How computers really work, built from scratch in C++.

item.title: From Brain to Equifax: 4 cyberattacks that changed computing
item.description: How the Brain virus, the Morris worm, ILOVEYOU and the Equifax breach worked, why each one spread, and what it changed for the people who build software.

item.title: 27 projects every senior engineer should build once
item.description: Twenty-seven hard projects, from an OS kernel and a compiler to a TCP/IP stack and a ray tracer, with what each one teaches you and where to start.

item.title: The Decorator pattern in modern C++
item.description: How the Decorator pattern adds behaviour to one object by wrapping it, shown with a C++20 coffee shop that uses unique_ptr, prices in pence and no duplicated members.

item.title: The Observer pattern in C++, without the lifetime bugs
item.description: How the Observer pattern lets one object notify many others, built as a C++20 weather station that uses weak_ptr so the subject never keeps dead observers alive.

item.title: The Strategy pattern in modern C++
item.description: How the Strategy pattern lets an object swap behaviour at runtime, shown with a C++20 example using std::unique_ptr, plus the lighter std::function version.

item.title: Object-oriented modelling, part 2: decomposition and generalization
item.description: How to split a system into parts with association, aggregation and composition, how inheritance generalizes shared behaviour, and how each one maps to C++ ownership.

item.title: Object-oriented modelling, part 1: abstraction and encapsulation
item.description: What abstraction and encapsulation mean in practice, how programming languages arrived at them, and how to show them in C++ code and UML class diagrams.
